changes_made.explanation: Removed duplicate 'Other:linguistic steganography' task and duplicate 'stegotext' output. Consolidated to single 'Other:Steganographic Text Generation' task which accurately describes the NLG task of generating text with embedded secret messages.

Removed duplicate metrics (Perplexity/PPL, JSD, BPW) and metrics that are actually LLM-as-judge criteria (Soundness, Relevance, Engagingness). Added the three JSD variants explicitly mentioned in the paper. Consolidated to unique, normalized metric names.

Normalized method name to 'pairwise sentence comparison' (more specific) and capitalized criteria names. Removed duplicate 'pairwise evaluation' method. The paper clearly uses GPT-3.5 to compare sentence pairs and score them on three quality dimensions.

No human evaluation is conducted in this paper. The authors explicitly use LLM-based evaluation (GPT-3.5) instead of human evaluation, as stated in Section 4.5: 'To simulate the human evaluation and ensure reproducibility, we conduct language evaluation on the generated stegotext of each method using large language models.'

overall_notes: The extraction was generally accurate. The paper focuses on steganographic text generation using LLMs, with comprehensive automatic evaluation (PPL, JSD variants, BPW, steganalysis) and LLM-as-judge evaluation using GPT-3.5. No human evaluation was conducted. The main corrections involved removing duplicates, separating automatic metrics from LLM-judge criteria, and normalizing names.
